newsitem.title: CHILE: Some Canadian investments subject to Chilean rule.
newsitem.headline: Some Canadian investments subject to Chilean rule.

text.p: Some Canadian financial investments will be subject to the 30 percent reserve requirement under the terms of a free trade deal worked out this week, a Chilean official said.

The agreement, to be initialed Monday in Ottawa by President Eduardo Frei and Canada's Prime Minister Jean Chretien, makes no change in reserve requirements for Canadian investors from those Central Bank announced last month, said the official who asked not to identified.

The 30 percent reserve requirement, known as the "encaje," will not be applied to productive investments, which in the case of Canada means mainly mining. But it still applies to capital inflows, said the official.
Reports from Ottawa had said Chile agreed to drop the "encaje" for all Canadian investments, but would leave it in place for a limited time on Canadian loans and credits.
It was not clear if there was some difference in interpretation of the agreement between the two sides, or whether there actually remained some discrepancy to be ironed out.
The Chilean official said there was no specific time limit on the reserve requirement for loans, but that the Central Bank could eventually reduce it.
Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat, on announcing the conclusion of the talks, had said Thursday there was no change in Chilean reserve requirements as applied to Canadians.
"Our currency measures have been preserved," he said, including also a one-year ban on capital repatriation. A spokesman said Aninat would not be available for comment until Friday afternoon.

Reviled by investors, the "encaje" is aimed at discouraging volatile, speculative capital from having undue influence on Chilean markets. But some economists say it effectively punishes productive and speculative investments alike.
